brief: Trace how minimum-only payments affect a balance under a supplied schedule.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Minimum Payments"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Sigue pagos de solo mínimo"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Acompanhe pagamentos de só mínimo"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Trace how minimum-only payments affect a balance under a supplied schedule.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: A minimum payment can leave debt and interest under the stated schedule; follow the balance rather than judging only punctuality.
instruction.misconception: An on-time minimum automatically prevents interest or clears debt.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use only the visible fictional amounts and conditions; earlier arithmetic is preparation, not a hidden financial assumption.

evidence.reasoning: Add the scheduled interest and fees, then subtract payments. Use the supplied order and check what debt remains.
Both minimum payments leave debt and scheduled interest.
The supplied schedule includes interest despite timely minimum payments.
The payment reduces the charged balance but does not clear it.
The larger payment leaves less debt under this schedule.
A short supplied schedule does not define every future balance.
Both minimums reduce debt but leave the stated remaining balance.
I checked: payment was incomplete. These terms still charge interest.
